Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  Progressive numbness/tingling and subjective weakness of left arm (elbow to palmar aspect of 2nd–4th digits) for ~2 weeks; transient 20-min loss of part of visual field in left eye a few weeks ago; occasional fatigue-type headaches; recent severe “cold/flu-like” illness; participates in new boxing classes (possible overuse/trauma).  
- Relevant family medical history:  Father – hypothyroidism and unspecified autoimmune condition; Mother – type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia; no known familial neurological disease.  
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  Ibuprofen PRN (dose/route/frequency not documented); Vitamin D (dose not documented); Iron supplement intermittently (dose not documented); Melatonin PRN (dose not documented).  
- Immunisation status reviewed:  Not recorded.  
- Sexual and reproductive health:  Not recorded.  
- Physical activity and nutrition:  Regular workouts and boxing classes; nutrition not discussed.  
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:  Occasional binge drinking (“partying until late”); smoking and other substance use not recorded.  
- Hearing loss or concerns:  Not recorded.  
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):  Expressed worry about possible diagnosis; no screening for depression or self-harm recorded.  
- Vision problems or recent changes:  Transient left-eye visual field loss ~20 min; no glasses/contact lenses; vision currently normal.  
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:  Not recorded.

- Mammogram (if eligible):  Not recorded.  
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D):  Not recorded.  

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 46-year-old right-handed woman with 2-week progressive left-arm sensory loss/weakness (palmar 2nd–4th digits, extends to elbow), minor shoulder discomfort with movement, transient monocular visual disturbance, recent viral illness, no objective exam or vitals yet.

Working differential:
• Cervical radiculopathy (C7) – plausible dermatomal distribution, temporal link to boxing (neck strain).  
• Median nerve entrapment – palmar 2nd–4th digit involvement and repetitive wrist impact.  
• Multiple sclerosis – separate neuro events (optic disturbance + limb sensory deficit) in middle-aged female, post-viral; considered higher-risk and prompted urgent referral.  

Plan: Urgent neurology referral arranged for MRI brain/spine and specialist assessment to confirm/exclude demyelinating disease or other central lesions. No pharmacologic treatment started. Safety-net advice: attend Emergency Department if weakness progresses to legs, new headaches, vomiting, seizures, or persistent/worsening visual symptoms.

Management Plan

- Urgent neurology referral (requested during consult) for MRI and further evaluation.  
- No steroids or disease-modifying therapy initiated pending definitive diagnosis.  
- Continue usual analgesia (ibuprofen PRN) if needed; avoid further strenuous boxing until evaluated.  
- Red-flag advice as above; patient advised to seek immediate care if symptoms escalate.  
- Follow-up: Await neurology appointment; primary care review after imaging or sooner if deterioration.

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  mental_health_support_or_not_recorded  
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Cervical radiculopathy (C7) – Medium-High likelihood: Dermatomal arm symptoms following neck/shoulder strain from boxing.  
2. Median nerve entrapment – Medium likelihood: Classic palmar 2nd–4th digit numbness with repetitive wrist impact, though proximal arm involvement less typical.  
3. Multiple sclerosis – Medium likelihood: Separate neurologic events (transient optic disturbance and unilateral limb sensory deficit) in 46-year-old woman with recent viral illness and family autoimmune history.

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs, neurological examination findings, BMI/weight, smoking status, immunisation review, mental health screening, cardiovascular risk screening (lipids, BGL), urinalysis, cervical screening status.  
● Internal contradictions: Patient initially answered “Yes, absolutely” to neck-pain question then immediately “No, nothing” – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear, but some overlapping speech and minor ambiguities; no physical examination possible via tele-consultation.
